title: Virtualization for large lists
description: Learn about Virtualization for large lists. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Virtualization (also called windowing) is a technique for efficiently rendering large lists by only rendering the items currently visible to the user. This dramatically reduces DOM nodes and improves performance for lists with thousands or millions of items.
The Performance Problem with Large Lists

Rendering a list with 10,000 items creates 10,000 DOM nodes, which causes significant performance issues: excessive memory usage, slow rendering, janky scrolling, and browser crashes. Virtualization solves this by maintaining a small window of rendered items.

data.title: Performance Impact Comparison
data.code:
Traditional List (10,000 items):
- DOM nodes: 10,000 elements
- Memory: ~50-100MB
- Initial render: 2-5 seconds
- Scroll performance: Poor (janky)
- Browser impact: High CPU/memory usage

Virtualized List (10,000 items):
- DOM nodes: ~20-30 elements (visible window)
- Memory: ~5-10MB
- Initial render: 100-200ms
- Scroll performance: Smooth (60fps)
- Browser impact: Minimal CPU/memory usage

data.text: Virtualization maintains a small window of visible items plus a buffer above and below. As the user scrolls, items leaving the window are unmounted and new items entering are mounted. The scroll position is mathematically calculated to maintain the illusion of a full list.

data.title: Virtualization Window Concept
data.code:
Virtualization Window Structure:

[Buffer: 5 items]  <-- Pre-rendered but not visible
[Visible: 10 items] <-- Actually visible to user
[Buffer: 5 items]  <-- Pre-rendered but not visible

Total rendered: 20 items
Total list: 10,000 items
Performance improvement: 500x fewer DOM nodes

Scroll Behavior:
- User scrolls down → Top items unmount, bottom items mount
- Scroll position calculated mathematically
- Scrollbar represents full list height
- User perceives normal scrolling experience

data.text: react-window is a lightweight, modern library for virtualizing lists. It provides several components for different use cases: FixedSizeList for uniform item heights, VariableSizeList for variable heights, and FixedSizeGrid for 2D virtualization.

data.text: react-virtualized is an older but feature-rich alternative. It provides more components and options but is larger and less actively maintained. Use react-window for new projects unless you need specific react-virtualized features.

data.title: Accessibility Considerations
data.text: Virtualized lists require special accessibility handling. Ensure proper ARIA roles, keyboard navigation, and screen reader support. Use libraries that include accessibility features or implement them manually.
Monitor virtualized list performance to ensure it's actually improving your application. Measure render times, scroll frame rates, and memory usage before and after implementation.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Virtualization reduces DOM nodes from thousands to dozens for large lists
Use react-window for modern, lightweight virtualization implementation
Choose FixedSizeList for uniform heights, VariableSizeList for variable heights
Implement infinite scroll by monitoring scroll position and loading more data
Memoize row components and use itemKey for optimal performance
Consider accessibility when implementing virtualized lists
Monitor performance to validate virtualization improvements
data.takeaway: Virtualization is essential for large lists, transforming performance-killing DOM-heavy lists into smooth, memory-efficient interfaces.
